rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the opinion to himself to deliver a narrow, unanimous statutory holding grounded in Missouri v. Hunter/Blockburger and the negative-implication evidence from § 924(c)’s explicit cumulation language, with Lora supporting that § 924(j) has its own penalty scheme. The most likely separate writings would be Gorsuch (lenity/separation-of-powers emphasis) or Thomas/Alito (textual/structural gloss or limiting language), but the strong 9-0 alignment makes additional opinions less likely overall.
